claims.text: Selective outward diffusion of passivating elements is the primary governor of protective-scale formation and persistence in CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
Al diffuses from the alloy subsurface to the surface and forms Al2O3.
Si preferentially diffuses to the surface and forms silica.
Surface Al2O3 is thin, continuous, coherent, adherent, and slow-growing enough to impede further oxygen ingress.
Surface silica is thin, continuous, coherent, adherent, and slow-growing enough to impede further oxygen ingress.
Mn has high mobility and a strong tendency to form oxides during high-temperature exposure.
Outward transport and oxidation of Mn can deplete Mn beneath the oxide scale.
Mn depletion can cause pore formation and accelerate oxide growth.
Mn produces non-protective oxides in CrMnFeCoNi.
Rapid Mn-oxide growth produces thick, incoherent scales that crack and spall.
CrFeCoNiAl alloys will form thin, uniform, adherent scales that remain stable during prolonged exposure above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiSi alloys will form thin, uniform, adherent scales that remain stable during prolonged exposure above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiMn alloys will form thicker, irregular, unstable scales prone to cracking and spallation.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C in both oxidative and corrosive atmospheres and in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Processing history and phase distribution can modulate oxidation behavior.
Replacing X with Al, Si, or Mn under otherwise identical processing provides the controlled comparison.
A CrFeCoNi alloy with a low concentration of Mn or passivating elements is the baseline control.
Equivalent protection by the Mn alloy, or substantial cracking or spallation of the Al and Si alloys, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The scoped materials are equiatomic or near-equiatomic CrFeCoNiX alloys, whereas the baseline is described as having a low concentration of Mn or passivators. It is therefore not clearly part of the stated initial-state population.

The intervention and experiment compare three X-substituted alloys directly, but the stated baseline is a separate, compositionally undefined low-X alloy that is not included in the experimental design.
